newsitem.title: USA: Photran CEO resigns, financial probe underway.
newsitem.headline: Photran CEO resigns, financial probe underway.

text.p: Photran Corp said Monday that David Stevenson, president, chief executive officer and a director, resigned, and the company is conducting an internal investigation of certain financial and accounting irregularities.
Kathleen Stevenson, corporate secretary and a director, aso resigned, effective immediatly.
Photran said it may restate the interim results for 1996 upon the conclusion of the investigation. It also expects to report a loss for the fourth quarter and the fiscal year ended December 31, 1996.
The company said Steven King, a member of the Photran board, and other directors assumed management responsibility for the company, aided by Photran's management team.

"The board has taken rapid action based on what we currently know, and we will update shareholders as soon as our investigation is completed," King said in a statement. "Our business fundamentals remain sound, we have solid customer commitments, and our coating process technology continues to position us well in the strengthening market for ITO coated glass."
No further details were immediately available.
Once the company's investigation is complete, it may restate its previously issued 1996 interim financial statements, Photran said.
Until such restatements, if any, have been filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, previously issued interim financial statements should not be relied upon, the company said.

It previously reported earnings for the first nine months of 1996 of $391,099 or $0.09 a share on sales of $4,862,105. This compared with a year-ago loss of $268,712 or $0.08 a share on sales of $2,107,146 for the nine-month 1995 period.
Photran said it and its consultants are working to complete their investigation as soon as possible.

Photran develops, manufactures and markets high performance optical and electrically conducive thin film coated products using a proprietary process technology known as Fuzion planar magnetron sputtering. The company produces products for the flat panel display industry.

In a statement, Paul Fink, chief financial officer, said the market for ITO coated glass continues to strengthen. He noted that Wintek Corp, the company's main customer, last week confirmed its intention to purchase one million pieces of ITO coated glass.

In meetings with Photran management, Wintek also confirmed its commitment to purchase an ITO coating line and to pay Photran to operate that equipment at the company's Lakeville, Minn., manufacturing facility through 1997.
Wintek also indicated its intention to place additional orders for ITO coated glass in 1997 and 1998, Fink said.
